“In the past, I was a deer-hunter in the forest wilderness;
having seen a green pāṭali tree, I— ”
I scattered three flowers. Then,
picking up the fallen leaves,
I discarded them outside.
Pure within and pure without,
well-liberated and free from taints—
just as if the Fully Awakened One were standing before one’s very eyes.
Having paid homage to Vipassī, the leader of the world, at the Pāṭalī tree,
I passed away there.
In the ninety-first aeon,
because I worshipped the Bodhi tree,
I do not know a state of misery.
This is the fruit of the worship of enlightenment.
There were thirteen kings named Samantapāsādika.
In this thirty-third aeon,
there were powerful wheel-turning monarchs.
The four analytical knowledges—
the Buddha's teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the Venerable Elder Tipupphiya speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Tipupphiya is the sixth.
